newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada threatens action against U.S. salmon fleet.
newsitem.headline: Canada threatens action against U.S. salmon fleet.

text.p: Canada announced on Wednesday that it had suspended salmon negotiations with the United States and would enforce restrictions against U.S. fishing vessels travelling through its waters.

A government statement said Fisheries Department staff had been instructed to enforce existing regulations requiring foreign vessels to contact Canadian authorities as they pass through Canadian waters -- or face possible arrest.
"We are deeply disappointed that the United States came to these meetings lacking the authority to negotiate," Foreign Minister Lloyd Axworthy said in a statement.
"Canada will resume negotiations as soon as the United States is prepared to negotiate in good faith. I will be pressing the U.S. government to ensure that its negotiator has a full mandate."

The government statement said: "Talks halted unexpectedly when the U.S. negotiator was unable to advance a position on one of the key southern issues, Fraser River sockeye. Until then the talks had been fairly positive."

The two countries have been arguing for years over how to divide up dwindling salmon stocks, amid accusations of overfishing. The measures announced on Wednesday fell short of those of 1994, when Canada imposed stiff fees on U.S. vessels heading for the Alaskan fishery from their base in Seattle.
